passage: Sunday morning in the hostel common room, Darshan set out a large mug of tea, his laptop and a folder of screenshots, and told his friend Karthik, "Today I do all the write-ups. All of them." "All six?" "All six. One sitting." In the earlier weeks, he had written a paragraph here, a paragraph there between assignments, and each time had to remember what the project did. This time he opened all the projects in a row, took the screenshots, wrote three lines about each, and named each file the same way. Karthik brought samosas at noon. By four o'clock the six summaries were done, and the page looked like a single piece of work instead of six.

qa.q: How many project write-ups did Darshan plan to finish that Sunday?
qa.a: Darshan planned to finish all six write-ups.

qa.q: How does Darshan feel by four o'clock?
qa.a: Darshan seems satisfied and relieved, since the six summaries are done and the page looks whole.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Darshan use for future projects, and why?
qa.a: Darshan could write a short note and take a screenshot as each project ends, because a small habit stops a big backlog from building up.

qa.q: How does Karthik see Darshan's Sunday plan?
qa.a: Karthik double-checks that all six will be done and brings samosas at noon, so Karthik supports the effort with company and food.

grounding: Shows setting aside one Sunday to write every project summary and capture screenshots in one sitting, which is quicker than fitting them between assignments.

passage:
Hi Leela,
You asked how I finally finished my portfolio after putting it off all semester. The trick was stupidly simple: I stopped doing it in bits.
Before, I'd write half a project summary between assignments, lose the thread, and start again the next week. Screenshots were worse: I'd open one project, take one picture, then get pulled into a lab report.
So I blocked last Sunday, 9 to 5, phone in the drawer. Morning: I wrote all four summaries back to back, same format, and they came out more consistent than anything I'd done in pieces. After lunch: I ran each project once and took all the screenshots in one go, same window size, same zoom. By 4:30 everything was uploaded.
Four months of 'I'll do it later', finished in one day.
Try it before your placement season starts.
Kunal

qa.q: Which hours did Kunal block on Sunday?
qa.a: 9 to 5, with the phone in the drawer.

qa.q: How does Kunal seem to feel about finishing in one day?
qa.a: Kunal sounds relieved and a little embarrassed that four months of putting it off were solved by such a simple trick.

qa.q: What would you change first if a whole Sunday were not possible for Leela?
qa.a: Block two shorter sessions, one only for writing and one only for screenshots, so each kind of task is still done in one run.

qa.q: How might Leela read this letter before placement season?
qa.a: Leela may feel encouraged, seeing a concrete plan from a friend who struggled with the same delay.

grounding: Shows a student setting aside one Sunday to write every project summary and take all the screenshots at once, finishing work that had dragged on in bits.

passage:
Madhav, you keep asking why my portfolio suddenly got done. Okay, confession from your friend Yusuf: I was doing it all wrong.
Every evening after assignments I'd try to write one project summary. Twenty minutes, then a quiz came up or someone called me for tea, and next time I'd reread everything and start over. Three weeks, one summary. Screenshots? I'd take one, then the next day the window was a different size and nothing matched.
Then my sister said, 'Do all of one kind of thing at once.' So I kept one Sunday completely free. Morning, only writing: all five summaries, one after another. Afternoon, only screenshots, same window, same zoom, twenty-two pictures. Evening, upload. Done by seven.
One day did what three weeks couldn't. So yes, block your Sunday. I'll bring the tea.

qa.q: How many screenshots were taken in the afternoon?
How did Yusuf feel during the three weeks of one summary, and what shows it?
qa.a: Yusuf was likely frustrated and stuck, rereading everything and starting over each time, and now calls it a confession of doing it all wrong.

qa.q: What else could help Yusuf keep the portfolio up to date later?
qa.a: Add each new project on the same kind of batch day once a month, instead of slipping back into small bits between assignments.

qa.q: What would change for Madhav with the same Sunday plan?
qa.a: Madhav could finish in one day what might otherwise drag on for weeks, with Yusuf keeping company over tea.

grounding: Shows a student keeping one Sunday for all project summaries and screenshots, which works far faster than doing them in bits between assignments.
